headline: First graded retrieval evaluation. The labels are mine, not a human assessor's.

setup.queries: 14 test-split queries, AI-authored, held out from any tuning
setup.catalog: 600 generated seed products, not a real assortment
setup.embeddings: deterministic bag-of-words hashing stub, NOT a trained model
setup.pool: 271 query/product pairs, blinded (no rank, mode, score or split shown)

what_this_supports: hybrid_rrf ranked highest on every metric, but its advantage over lexical text search is not distinguishable from zero: the bootstrap interval spans -0.21 to +0.30 over 9 families.

Five of fourteen queries had no relevant product in the pool at all, so NDCG is null for them and only nine are scorable. Two are genuine recall failures: the catalog contains walking/running shoes and a beard trimmer, and neither was retrieved for the query that wanted them.
what_this_does_not_support: Any claim about semantic search quality. The embedding service was a hashing stub, so the vector and RRF numbers measure a bag-of-words hash, not a trained model. vector scoring 0.3888 against text at 0.7368 says nothing about a real embedding model.
Any claim about shopper relevance. The queries are AI-authored and the labels are AI-assigned; no human judged anything.
Any comparison with the older catalog-derived metrics (P@10 .9457 / NDCG@10 .9574). Those used binary labels derived from the same rows that generated the queries.
Generalisation to a real assortment. 600 generated products with formulaic variants is not a catalog.
reproduce: ops/evaluation/collect-run.sh, then graded_eval.py evaluate --assessor claude-opus-5 --split test
